# Inner Niger Delta staff gauges and provenance

`staff_stage.csv` contains published stage observations from Mali’s Direction nationale de l'hydraulique (DNH), the regional service in Tombouctou, and the OPIDIN operating team. Each row names a source in `source_receipts.json`, with a direct URL, the retrieved byte count, SHA-256, and a locator. Stage is centimetres relative to each station’s own gauge zero. Compare changes within a station. For Sélingué the bulletin lists centimetres on a reservoir elevation scale. No time of day, gauge-zero survey uncertainty or stage precision beyond the reported digits is provided.

Daily rows in the DNH weekly tables are dated observations. A table for 2026 also reports the previous year's stage for the same month and day. A plus sign is the agency's missing-value symbol. Those cells are omitted. Decadal values in GTPA are averages over the 10 or 11 days indicated. The two terminal-date entries from the Tombouctou service use the dated descriptions accompanying the graphics. The bimonthly rows use the published period mean. Historical values under “H Moyenne” in weekly bulletins and “Moy” in GTPA have month-day bounds and no year. The averaging period is unspecified there. No stage has been imputed to match an overpass.

## Comparable rise and recession

| Observation support | Mopti, m | Diré, m | Source |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| 21–31 July 2024, 11-day mean | 3.41 | 1.15 | GTPA table 3, prior-year column |
| 26 January 2025, daily | 3.15 | 5.58 | DNH no. 04/2026, prior-year column |
| 13 July 2025, daily | 2.82 | 1.66 | DNH no. 28/2026, prior-year column |
| 19 January 2026, daily | 2.85 | 5.15 | DNH no. 03/2026 |
| 13 July historical mean | 2.00 | 0.98 | DNH no. 28/2026 |
| 19 January historical mean | 1.95 | 3.63 | DNH no. 03/2026 |

For the first pair, recession minus rise gives +4.43 m at Diré and −0.26 m at Mopti. For the second pair the differences are +3.49 m and +0.03 m. At the time of the second mid-January SWOT visit, the nearest bracketing staff observations were 12 and 19 January 2026. The gauge readings establish the phase-dependent spatial contrast at the stations. They do not measure satellite-reach discharge. The late-arriving flood wave and wetland attenuation have been studied previously. [Inner Niger Delta flood-model study](https://doi.org/10.1029/2021MS002463) · [OPIDIN technical background](https://opidin.org/en/background/technical-background-opidin)

## Annual maxima

The OPIDIN API snapshot contains 119 consecutive flood seasons, 1907–2025, for Mopti, Akka and Diré. Use `data[*].year` as the flood-season label. The typical season runs June through the following spring. The API does not contain peak dates, per-row source flags, datum changes, or uncertainty. The contemporaneous OPIDIN bulletin dated the 2024 Mopti crest to 8 November. Its December predictions for downstream crest timing cannot serve as measured dates. For 2025 the October bulletin reported a 642 cm crest to date while the API lists a final 662 cm. The reason for the difference is unresolved. [Annual maxima](https://backend.opidin.org/opidin/rest/annualmaxlevels) · [2024 bulletin](https://opidin.org/en/news/bulletins-2024/bulletin-19-18-november-2024) · [2025 bulletin archive](https://opidin.org/fr/news?b_start%3Aint=0&set_language=fr)

OPIDIN states that daily gauging started in 1922 at Mopti, 1931 at Diré, and 1955 at Akka. OPIDIN’s forecast page notes reconstruction of historical maxima before 1955. A 2009 hydrometric audit identifies changes to both Mopti and Diré staff gauges in 1949. Treat records preceding 1955 separately. Sahel Rain Index reports that daily Akka measurements were unavailable starting in 2019. A separate 2024 study reports that its Akka in situ series ends in 2018. The provenance of subsequent Akka maxima in the API is unresolved. Exclude those entries from historical tests requiring a directly observed Akka stage. [OPIDIN](https://opidin.org/en/floodviewer/flood-forecast) · [Historical gauge audit](https://horizon.documentation.ird.fr/exl-doc/pleins_textes/divers11-03/010047094.pdf) · [Sahel Rain Index methods](https://sahelrainindex.info/methods-data/) · [Water extent and storage study](https://doi.org/10.1080/10106049.2024.2311203)

The staff-gauge comparisons above concern local stage and SWOT geometry. A physical sensor independent of KaRIn can share gauge lineage with the gauge-constrained discharge model. Discharge validation additionally requires an independent discharge observation with station, period, rating and assimilation lineage documented. The near-date discharge comparisons below use the agency’s current-year discharge column.

## Unconstrained discharge against agency bulletin flows

The first ten DNH weekly bulletins of 2024 report a discharge in m³/s alongside the current dated stage at Mopti and Diré. The 2026 bulletins include previous-year stage and current-year discharge. In particular, the 26 January 2026 bulletin gives **stage only** for 26 January 2025. An original, dated 2025 discharge for that pass could not be verified. The January–March 2024 series is preserved in `dnh_2024_discharge.csv` with row-level source IDs. DNH supplies a calendar date for each daily reference flow. The overpass is instantaneous, and the agency does not specify time of day, uncertainty, direct current-meter gauging, or rating curve version in the tables.

`dnh_l4_near_dates.csv` pairs each archived L4 overpass at the two primary reaches with the closest available bulletin day within two calendar days. Earlier dates break ties. The filter retains a ratio for positive, non-fill consensus Q and reach quality 0 or 1. It preserves missing results as empty cells. All eight usable pairs had quality 1 (“suspect”) and were 1–2 calendar days apart. Both records in each pair refer to the same season and location corridor. Gauge cross-section, contributing branches, retrieval quality, and offset during the rapidly declining flow matter. On the 17 January 2024 pass near Diré the consensus was 3,391 m³/s compared with 1,357 m³/s on 15 January; near Mopti the corresponding values were 2,111 and 327 m³/s. Across four usable pairs per station the ratios (satellite/agency) ranged from 2.14–4.48 at Diré and 3.70–33.65 at Mopti. These external measurements give no support for interpreting the absolute L4 discharges as verified flow changes.

The unconstrained branch uses uncalibrated Water Balance Model priors, and the gauge-constrained branch can incorporate historical and concurrent flow data. No constrained series enters the comparison. The 2024 DNH values provide external reference estimates for the unconstrained product by design. An audit of individual model configuration, rating curves and gauge overlap for the constrained branch remains unavailable here. [Discharge framework, section 3.3](https://doi.org/10.1029/2021WR031614) · [NASA v3 collection and product guide](https://podaac.jpl.nasa.gov/dataset/SWOT_L4_HR_DAWG_SOS_DISCHARGE_V3)
